title: A uniform bound for proper direct image
statement:
Use the universe and small-site convention of [def-weil-size-convention]; all filtered diagrams and families are small in its chosen universe. Use the standing scheme setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p_0>0$ with $p_0\ne\ell$, and separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $k$-morphisms. The field $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]; $\Qlb$ has the condensed coefficient meaning of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Sheaves below are module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] for the pulled-back ring $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Write $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ for constructible sheaves [sk-def-sfb-constructible] and $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$ for their filtered colimits in the ambient module category, as in clause (2) of [det-ind-heart-full-faithfulness]. Here $R^qp_*M=\mathcal H^q(Rp_*(M[0]))$, using the module-object derived direct image [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Properness is [def-weil-proper-morphism], geometric fibres are [def-weil-geometric-fibre], and dimension means the Krull dimension of the underlying topological space [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$. Let $p\colon X\to Y$ be proper, and let $d$ be an integer bounding the dimensions
of all geometric fibres of $p$ (for instance $d=\dim X$). For $M\in\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$
([det-ind-heart-full-faithfulness]),

$$
R^qp_*M=0\quad(q>2d+1),\qquad R^qp_*M\in\IndCons(Y,\Lambda)\quad(q\geq0),
$$

and $R^qp_*\colon\IndCons(X,\Lambda)\to\IndCons(Y,\Lambda)$ preserves arbitrary direct sums.

The proof computes with an integral lattice. Its reductions modulo $\pi_E^n$ satisfy the classical
torsion bound $2d$, and the derived inverse limit over $n$ costs one more degree, whence $2d+1$.

proof.text: The proper map $p$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Indeed [def-weil-proper-morphism] makes it finite type and separated. Finite type includes quasi-compactness by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Its diagonal is a closed immersion; by the affine-open description in [def-weil-closed-immersion] the inverse image of any affine open under that diagonal is affine, hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. This is precisely quasi-separatedness in [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Thus the qcqs hypothesis for the continuity theorem below is satisfied. The schemes $X$ and $Y$ are also Noetherian, as required by the current statement of [det-ind-heart-full-faithfulness]. Indeed every ideal of the field $k$ is either zero or generated by $1$, so $k$ is Noetherian by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The single affine chart of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ makes it locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth], and it is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to each of the finite-type structure morphisms $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ from the standing setting. This verifies local Noetherianity and quasi-compactness without adding a hypothesis to the item.

source.place: Final paragraph: the qcqs hypothesis of the continuity input, expanded from the properness hypothesis.; Stacks 01OV (definition-noetherian), 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), for the updated ind-realization hypotheses

proof.text: For every $C\in\Cons(X,\Lambda)$, apply the already existing same-unit intermediate [det-proper-heart-bound-rational] to this $p$ and $d$. Its statement gives $R^qp_*C=0$ for every $q>2d+1$, uniformly in $C$. The intermediate is the constructible case of the source: its dependency chain is the reduction to lattices, the torsion bound, the Milnor bound, and passage to rational coefficients. We take precisely its stated constructible vanishing, not any construction from its proof.

source.place: First five paragraphs (unit steps 1–5), assembled by the existing det-proper-heart-bound-rational intermediate.

proof.text: For $C\in\Cons(X,\Lambda)$, the complex $C[0]$ lies in $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ by the definition [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: its only nonzero cohomology is $C$ in degree zero. Clause (2) of [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-rational] applies to the proper map between the standing schemes and gives $Rp_*C[0]\in\Dbc(Y,\Lambda)$. Unpacking the same definition, each $R^qp_*C=\mathcal H^q(Rp_*C[0])$ is in $\Cons(Y,\Lambda)$. This establishes the constructible target statement separately from the uniform bound.

source.place: Final paragraph, first sentence: proper direct image preserves bounded constructible complexes.

proof.text: Apply [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] on $X$ and $Y$, and also to the ring object $p_*\Lambda_X$ on $Y$. The size convention is that of the statement; abelian sheafification and its monoidal structure are supplied by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Denote the resulting section-ring sheaves by $A=\Lambda_X$, $B=\Lambda_Y$ and $p_*A$, retaining their non-discrete coefficient meaning. The equivalences are additive because they are the identity on underlying sheaves and maps, so addition of maps is unchanged. By [lem-weil-pbc-equivalence-injective-resolutions] they preserve kernels, cokernels, all small colimits, and injective resolutions. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], forgetting the sectionwise module structure is faithful and exact and preserves small colimits. In particular restriction along $B\to p_*A$ preserves cohomology and small colimits: the canonical comparisons become identities of the corresponding underlying abelian sheaves. A bijective linear sheaf map has a linear inverse, since $u(rv)=ru(v)$ implies $u^{-1}(rw)=ru^{-1}(w)$. These observations also show that such comparisons are isomorphisms of modules, not just abelian sheaves.

source.place: Final paragraph: coefficient-category and scalar-restriction bookkeeping for applying continuity; Stacks 00YV, 015Z, 03DA, 03DB.

proof.text: For a module object $N$ on $X$, choose a bounded-below injective resolution $\Phi_XN[0]\to J$ in sectionwise $A$-modules by [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution]. Transport it back through the additive equivalence of step 4. By [lem-weil-pbc-equivalence-injective-resolutions] this gives a bounded-below complex $I$ of injective internal modules resolving $N[0]$. There are enough injectives internally because the equivalence transports the resolutions that exist for every sectionwise module. Thus $I$ is K-injective by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. The sectionwise complex $J$ is K-injective by the resolution statement itself. Now [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] computes $Rp_*N[0]$ on $I$. Its underived functor is the composite in [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]: its underlying complex is $p_*^{\mathrm{Ab}}I$, with action restricted along $B\to p_*A$. The sectionwise direct image in [det-proper-heart-continuity-direct-image] computes on $J$ and has underlying complex $p_*^{\mathrm{Ab}}J$. The equivalence identifies these complexes and their differentials. Exactness from step 4 therefore identifies their cohomology after scalar restriction. This identification is natural: the resolution-transport statement also transports lifts of morphisms and homotopies. It consequently identifies the legs, and hence the universal comparison maps, for filtered colimits and sums. We may apply both continuity assertions to the module-object $R^qp_*$ used here.

source.place: Final paragraph: identifying the two derived direct images before applying continuity; Stacks 07A5, 079P, 015Z, 070J.

proof.text:
Let $M\in\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$. The Noetherianity of $X$ and $Y$ was verified in step 1, and all diagrams are small in the stated size convention. Clause (2) of [det-ind-heart-full-faithfulness] supplies a small filtered diagram $(C_\alpha)_{\alpha\in I}$ of constructible sheaves with $M\cong\varinjlim_\alpha C_\alpha$ in the ambient module category. Apply [det-proper-heart-continuity-direct-image], using the qcqs hypothesis from step 1 and the comparison in steps 4–5. For every $q$ this gives the canonical isomorphism
$$R^qp_*M\cong\varinjlim_{\alpha\in I}R^qp_*C_\alpha.$$
Each term on the right is constructible by step 3; clause (2) of [det-ind-heart-full-faithfulness] on $Y$ therefore makes this colimit an object of $\IndCons(Y,\Lambda)$. If $q>2d+1$, every term is zero by step 2. The universal property of the colimit of a zero diagram gives a zero object, proving the required vanishing.

source.place: Final paragraph, second sentence: filtered-colimit passage to IndCons, including membership and vanishing.

proof.text:
Let $(M_s)_{s\in S}$ be any small family in $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$. The ambient sum $\bigoplus_sM_s$ belongs to $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$ by [det-ind-heart-filtered-colimits]. Step 6 puts each $R^qp_*M_s$ and $R^qp_*(\bigoplus_sM_s)$ in $\IndCons(Y,\Lambda)$; the same closure statement on $Y$ puts $\bigoplus_sR^qp_*M_s$ there. The direct-sum assertion of [det-proper-heart-continuity-direct-image], with qcqs from step 1 and the comparison of steps 4–5, gives
$$\bigoplus_{s\in S}R^qp_*M_s\xrightarrow{\sim}R^qp_*\left(\bigoplus_{s\in S}M_s\right).$$
By clause (2) of [det-ind-heart-full-faithfulness], each $\IndCons$ is full and replete in its ambient module category. Hence the displayed ambient isomorphism and its inverse are morphisms in $\IndCons$. An ambient sum belonging to this full subcategory satisfies its coproduct universal property there: a family of maps into an object of the subcategory extends uniquely in the ambient category, and fullness keeps that extension in the subcategory. This proves preservation of arbitrary direct sums by the restricted $R^qp_*$, including the empty sum.

source.place: Final paragraph, final sentence: arbitrary direct sums and the full-subcategory coproduct property.

I read the item, all 34 cited statements, the unit record, the main-20261015 blueprint unit and proof, and the Stacks sources 01T6, 070J, 015Z, 03DA/03DB, 095U and 09A6. The statement is word for word the blueprint's: Λ=E or Q̄_ℓ, p proper, fibre bound d, vanishing for q>2d+1, R^q p_* in IndCons, and preservation of direct sums. Edge cases hold: d<0 forces X empty, d=0 gives an upper bound only, q=2d+1 is not claimed, and the empty sum is fine. Step 1: qcqs follows from the proper, finite-type, closed-immersion and affine-qcqs nodes. X and Y are Noetherian by Stacks 01T6, as det-ind-heart-full-faithfulness requires. Step 2 uses only the statement of the same-unit node det-proper-heart-bound-rational. Step 3 uses clause (2) of det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-rational, the blueprint's own step-6 input. I accept that tool use and found no DAG cycle in the full transitive closure. Steps 4–5 correctly identify internal Λ_X-modules with the sectionwise A-modules of det-proper-heart-continuity-direct-image. They use the internal/sectionwise equivalence, which is the identity on underlying sheaves, injective-resolution transport, bounded-below injective complexes being K-injective (Stacks 070J), and the exact, colimit-preserving forgetful functor. Restriction along Λ_Y→p_*Λ_X is handled, and naturality comes from transported lifts. Steps 6–7 apply clause (2) of the ind-heart node, the continuity clauses and closure under sums, with the coproduct in the full subcategory written out. Accepted tool uses: det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-rational, lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution, lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful; the ind-heart and continuity nodes are on the unit route. There are no new nodes. The duplicate det-proper-heart-bound-indcons is correctly in same_as and not used as a dependency.
